mainTopic: צאן ברזל generations, an animal that looks like a different species from its mother (בכורה, קרבנות, wool and wine), and twin male firstborns
overview: The amud opens by finishing the argument between רב הונא and רב יהודה about how many generations of צאן ברזל animals are exempt from בכורה. Each side reads רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's 'even ten generations' and the wording of the משנה so that it fits his own view. Next the גמרא turns to a ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal. רב אושעיא brings a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר says such an animal is obligated and חכמים say it is exempt. The גמרא tests what 'obligated' could mean and then explains the argument through several possible cases, including רב אשי's case of an animal with only some of its mother's features. רבי יוחנן adds that even רבי מאיר requires the ראש חודש goat to be born from a goat, and the גמרא shows that both פסוקים about such animals are needed. Several אמוראים then compare wool to linen, which does not change, to rule that wool from such an animal is excluded from שעטנז, תכלת and נגעים. רב אשי extends the idea to wine from a vine grown over a fig tree. Finally a new משנה begins: twin male lambs born at the same moment, with opinions of רבי יוסי הגלילי, חכמים, רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל fit רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's phrase 'even until ten generations' fits רב יהודה's view that the first תנא already exempts more than one generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said to the first תנא: even up to ten generations, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב יהודה. It shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words make good sense according to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' suggests that the first תנא already exempted several generations, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל wants to go much further. That matches רב יהודה, who holds that the first תנא goes down more than one generation.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what [he] said; this explains why someone said it
Exempt (here, from the law of בכורה)

phrases.english: This is what ... said to him
phrases.notes: 'To him' means to the first תנא of the משנה. The גמרא is saying this line fits רב יהודה's view.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:
Even until ten generations, they are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the רב הונא and רב יהודה dispute from the previous daf by bringing support for רב יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's view that the first תנא exempts more than one generation
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's wording 'even until ten generations' in the משנה

steps.title: How does רב הונא explain 'even ten generations'?
steps.stepSummary: If the first תנא does not exempt any further generations, as רב הונא says, then the word 'even' in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement seems out of place.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב הונא, who says the first תנא does not go down into generations at all, what does 'even until ten generations' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. His reading seems to clash with the word 'even'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Even ten generations' only sounds natural if someone already exempted a few generations. According to רב הונא, the first תנא's first case exempts only the direct offspring, so who was going down into generations?

keyTerms.meaning: But according to ... (introduces a problem for the other opinion)
The first תנא, the unnamed opinion stated first
Goes down into generations, extending the rule to later generations
What is ...? What does it mean?

phrases.english: But according to Rav Huna, who says:
the first tanna does not go down into generations,
what is 'even until ten generations'?
phrases.notes: The problem is the word 'even'. It sounds like it builds on a first תנא who already exempted several generations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the support for רב יהודה into a difficulty for רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that the first תנא does not go down into generations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'even' in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement implies the first תנא already exempted several generations, which contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is responding to the העמיד case
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is reacting to the משנה's second case, where the Jew put the offspring in place of the mothers. In that case even the first תנא goes down into generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can tell you: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is talking about the case of 'he established [the offspring in place of the mothers]', where the first תנא does go down into generations.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends himself by moving רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's comment to a different part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second case (העמיד), the first תנא does exempt a later generation. So 'even ten generations' builds on that case, and רב הונא can still say the first case covers only one generation.

keyTerms.meaning: [He] can say to you (introduces how someone would defend himself)
He established; the משנה's case where the Jew put the offspring in place of the mothers
Is standing on, is referring to

phrases.english: Rav Huna can say to you:

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַ״הֶעֱמִיד״ קָאֵי
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is referring to 'he established'
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's second case, where the Jew put the offspring in place of the mother animals.

phrases.english: where [the first tanna] does go down into generations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the reference: the statement refers to a different clause of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was reacting to the first case, so the first תנא must already exempt several generations there.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is reacting to the העמיד case, where the first תנא does go down into generations. The first case can still be limited to one generation, as רב הונא says.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב הונא and רב יהודה can explain רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. For רב יהודה he builds on the first case, and for רב הונא he builds on the העמיד case.

steps.title: A version of the משנה that seems to refute רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's wording: 'the offspring are exempt, and the offspring of the offspring are not.' This seems to say directly that the second generation is obligated, against רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who accepts צאן ברזל animals from a gentile: the offspring are exempt, and the offspring of the offspring are not. This is a refutation of רב יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the wording of the משנה as a challenge to רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said the offspring of the offspring are also exempt. Read plainly, this wording says the opposite: only the direct offspring are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Iron flock': animals given under a deal where their value is guaranteed to the owner
Offspring of the offspring, the second generation

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who accepts 'iron flock' animals from a gentile —
phrases.notes: The Jew takes the animals to raise, but their value stays guaranteed to the gentile, so they are counted as the gentile's.

phrases.english: the offspring are exempt,
and the offspring of the offspring are not.
This is a refutation of Rav Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement has been explained both ways, the גמרא challenges רב יהודה from the wording of the first case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's view that the offspring of the offspring are also exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording states plainly that the offspring of the offspring are not exempt.

steps.title: רב יהודה reads 'offspring' as 'they and their offspring'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the exempt 'offspring' in the משנה should be understood as 'they and their offspring', so two generations are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה can tell you: read it as 'they and their offspring' are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה defends his view by reading the משנה's word 'offspring' more broadly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this reading, 'offspring' means the direct offspring together with their own offspring. The 'offspring of the offspring' that are not exempt are therefore one generation further down, and רב יהודה's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Say; read it this way (introduces a reinterpretation of the wording)

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful: in רב יהודה's answer, 'they' means the direct offspring, not the original mother animals. In רב הונא's answer in Step 7, 'they' means the mothers.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda can say to you:
Say: 'they and their offspring.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of רב יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Offspring are exempt' means only the direct offspring.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Offspring' means the offspring and their offspring. Only the generation after that is obligated.

steps.title: A second version of the משנה that seems to refute רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: Some report that the משנה actually reads 'they and their offspring are exempt.' This seems to exempt two generations, against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say the wording is: 'they and their offspring are exempt.' This is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of the exchange. Here the wording of the משנה itself challenges רב הונא instead of רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the text says 'they and their offspring', it sounds like two generations are exempt. That clashes with רב הונא, who limits the exemption to the direct offspring.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
They and their offspring are exempt,
phrases.notes: In this version these words are the actual text of the משנה, not רב יהודה's rereading.

phrases.english: a refutation of Rav Huna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version of Steps 4–5, in which the challenge is aimed at רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that only the direct offspring are exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'They and their offspring' seems to exempt two generations.

steps.title: רב הונא reads 'they' as the mother animals
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that 'they' means the original mother animals and 'offspring' means their direct offspring. Both are exempt, but the offspring of the offspring are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can tell you: read it as 'they and the offspring are exempt, and the offspring of the offspring are obligated.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends his view by explaining who 'they' refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'they' means the mother animals, then 'they and their offspring' covers only one generation of offspring. That is exactly רב הונא's view, so the second generation is obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligated (here, in the law of בכורה)
Offspring, the direct babies of the original animals

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the debate over the משנה's wording. In each one, the opinion being challenged survives by explaining who 'they' and 'offspring' refer to. For רב הונא one generation is exempt, and for רב יהודה two generations are exempt.

phrases.english: Rav Huna can say to you:
Say: they and the offspring — exempt,
phrases.notes: Here 'they' means the original mother animals themselves.

phrases.english: and the offspring of the offspring — obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of רב הונא in the second version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'They' means the offspring, so two generations are exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'They' means the mother animals, so only one generation of offspring is exempt and the next is obligated.

steps.title: A ewe born to a goat: רבי מאיר and חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about a ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal. רב אושעיא brings a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר obligates such an animal in בכורה and חכמים exempt it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A ewe that gave birth to a kind of goat, etc.' רב אושעיא came from נהרדעא and brought a ברייתא with him: A ewe born to a goat, or a goat born to a ewe: רבי מאיר obligates it, and חכמים exempt it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא quotes the משנה about an animal that looks like a different species from its mother, and רב אושעיא brings a ברייתא that shows a dispute about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reports an argument: רבי מאיר says such an animal is 'obligated,' and חכמים say it is exempt. The ברייתא does not say what 'obligated' refers to, and that is the question the next steps take up.

keyTerms.meaning: Kind, species; here an animal that looks like a different species
A ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: A ewe that gave birth to a kind of goat, etc.
Rav Oshaya came from Neharde'a,
and brought a baraita in his hand:
A ewe, daughter of a goat,
and a goat, daughter of a ewe —
Rabbi Meir obligates,
and the Rabbis exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the צאן ברזל discussion and opens the next topic of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal born to a mother of a different-looking species (a sheep born to a goat, or a goat born to a sheep): רבי מאיר says it is obligated in בכורה, and חכמים say it is exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא opens a long discussion. The גמרא first asks what רבי מאיר's 'obligated' means, then explains the argument through several possible cases (Steps 9–16).

steps.title: רב הושעיא asks what רבי מאיר obligates
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא asks רבה to find out from רב הונא which obligation רבי מאיר means in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said to רבה: When you go in to רב הונא, ask him: in what exactly does רבי מאיר obligate this animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a question about the ברייתא from the last step. It asks which מצוה רבי מאיר's word 'obligated' is talking about. The next steps will test the possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said רבי מאיר holds this ewe's goat-like offspring is 'obligated.' Each obvious meaning has a problem, so רב הושעיא wants רב הונא to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligates, holds it is subject to a מצוה
For what? In regard to what?

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said to Rabba:
When you go in before Rav Huna,
ask him:
Rabbi Meir obligates it in what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the ruling in the ברייתא of step 8 refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which obligation רבי מאיר means: בכורה, ראשית הגז, or something else.

steps.title: It cannot mean the firstborn מצוה
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר means בכורה, that clashes with the פסוק 'אך בכור שור.' That פסוק requires the firstborn to be the same kind as its mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he obligates it in בכורה: doesn't רבי מאיר accept the פסוק 'אך בכור שור,' which teaches that the mother must be an ox and its firstborn an ox?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible answer, בכורה, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אך בכור שור' teaches that בכורה applies only when the baby is the same kind as its mother. A goat-like baby born to a ewe does not fit that rule. So רבי מאיר would hardly obligate it in בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offering a possibility to test it)
The מצוה of a firstborn animal

phrases.english: If you say it is regarding the firstborn מצוה,
but doesn't Rabbi Meir hold of
"But the firstborn of an ox"
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:17

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא שׁוֹר וּבְכוֹרוֹ שׁוֹר?
phrases.english: only when it is an ox and its firstborn is an ox?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא לִבְכוֹרָה וְלֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to step 9's question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires the firstborn to match its mother. This baby does not match, so it should be exempt.

steps.title: It also cannot easily mean the first shearing
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר means ראשית הגז, there is a problem. דבי רבי ישמעאל taught that sheep with tough wool are exempt, and a goat-like animal has tough wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he means ראשית הגז. But doesn't he accept what דבי רבי ישמעאל taught: sheep with tough wool are exempt from ראשית הגז, as it says 'and he was warmed by the fleece of my sheep'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second answer, ראשית הגז, and finds a problem with it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only wool soft enough to keep a person warm counts for ראשית הגז. A goat-like animal has tough, goat-like hair. So it should be exempt from ראשית הגז as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The first shearing of wool, given to a כהן
The study house of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: Rather, it is regarding the first shearing of wool,
but doesn't he hold of
that which the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Sheep whose wool is tough
are exempt from the first shearing,
as it says: "and he was warmed by the fleece of my sheep"?
phrases.notes: איוב 31:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second possible answer after step 10 rejected the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רבי מאיר's 'obligated' as ראשית הגז
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tough wool is exempt because of the פסוק in איוב. A goat-like animal has tough wool, so it should be exempt.

steps.title: The dispute is about the father in the law of 'it and its offspring'
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains the case: the father is a male goat. רבי מאיר and רבנן argue whether the father's line counts for אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Let us look. What case are we dealing with? A ewe gave birth to a goat-like animal, and its father is a male goat. They argue about whether we worry about the father's line for אותו ואת בנו. רבי מאיר says we worry about the father's line. רבנן say we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question himself. 'Obligated' is not about בכורה or wool at all. It is about the איסור of slaughtering a parent and its young on the same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby looks like its goat father, so it is clearly that father's child. רבי מאיר says the father counts for אותו ואת בנו, so slaughtering the father and this baby on one day is forbidden. רבנן say only the mother counts.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
We take the father's line into account
The איסור of slaughtering an animal and its young on the same day

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'obligated' does not mean a מצוה to give something. It means you are liable if you slaughter the father and this baby on the same day.

phrases.english: He said to him: Let us see,
phrases.notes: This is רבה answering רב הושעיא himself.

phrases.english: here, what are we dealing with?
With a ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal,
and its father is a male goat,
and about whether we take the father's line into account
regarding "it and its offspring" they disagree,
phrases.notes: This is the rule against slaughtering an animal and its young on the same day.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Meir holds:
we take the father's line into account,
and the Rabbis hold:
we do not take the father's line into account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the problems in steps 10–11 by moving the ruling to a different law.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case and the law in question (הכא במאי עסקינן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Obligated' meant בכורה or ראשית הגז, and both run into problems.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Obligated' refers to אותו ואת בנו with the goat father. רבי מאיר counts the father's line; רבנן do not.

steps.title: Then why not argue about the father in general?
steps.stepSummary: If the argument is really about the father's line, the ברייתא should have said so plainly, like the known dispute of חנניה and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let them argue about the father's line in general, in the dispute of חנניה and רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבה's answer from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether the father counts for אותו ואת בנו is already argued in general by חנניה and רבנן. So why would the ברייתא tie it to the unusual case of a ewe giving birth to a goat-like animal? The ברייתא could simply have said רבי מאיר agrees with חנניה.

phrases.english: If so,
let them disagree about the father's line in general,
as in the dispute of Chananya and the Rabbis!
phrases.notes: That dispute appears in חולין 78b.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי לִיפַּלְגוּ בְּחוֹשְׁשִׁין לְזֶרַע הָאָב בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's explanation that the dispute is about the father's line
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general question would not be taught through a rare case. The ברייתא should have stated the general dispute of חנניה and רבנן.

steps.title: Back to firstborn: a ewe born to a ewe that came from a goat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the father-line idea and says רבי מאיר does mean בכורה. The case is a ewe whose mother is a ewe, but whose grandmother was a goat. רבי מאיר follows the mother, while חכמים follow the grandmother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it really is about the firstborn. The case is a ewe born to a ewe that was born to a goat. One view says: follow the mother, and this animal does not count as 'looking like a different kind.' The other view says: follow the mother's mother, and this animal does count as 'looking like a different kind.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the father-line explanation and returns to בכורה. It sets up a case where the newborn looks like its mother but not like its grandmother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the problem from Step 10. The פסוק 'אך בכור שור' wants the firstborn to match its mother, and here it does match its mother, so רבי מאיר obligates it. חכמים say the real test is the grandmother, and since this animal does not look like the grandmother, it counts as a 'look-alike' and is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (we go back to the first idea)
What case are we dealing with?
An animal that looks like a different species

steps.confusionAlert: Each 'בת' goes back one generation. The newborn is a ewe, its mother is a ewe, and its grandmother is a goat. The newborn matches its mother, not its grandmother.

phrases.english: Rather, it really is about the firstborn,
and here, what are we dealing with?
With a ewe, daughter of a ewe, daughter of a goat.
One master holds: follow its mother,
and this one is not a look-alike.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: זִיל בָּתַר אִימַּיהּ דְּאִימֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: And the other master holds: follow its mother's mother,
and this one is a look-alike.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם לִבְכוֹרָה, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the father-line answer that Step 13 attacked and goes back to the בכורה reading, now with a new case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי מאיר means בכורה, he would be obligating an animal that does not look like its mother, which goes against 'אך בכור שור.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The newborn does look like its mother. The argument is only about whether the grandmother also counts.

steps.title: Another case: a ewe born to a goat that came from a ewe
steps.stepSummary: A second way to set up the case: the newborn ewe's mother is a goat, and its grandmother is a ewe. The argument is whether the 'sheep nature' has returned to its original place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say the case is a ewe born to a goat that was born to a ewe. One view says: the sheep nature has returned to its place. The other view says: the sheep nature has not returned to its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different case that could explain the same argument. Here the newborn matches its grandmother but not its mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that once the newborn looks like a sheep again, like the original grandmother, it is fine and is obligated in בכורה. חכמים hold that the sheep nature has not truly come back, so the newborn simply does not match its mother and is exempt.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
with a ewe, daughter of a goat, daughter of a ewe,
one master holds: the sheep nature returned to its place,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לֹא חָזְרוּ שֵׂיֻיוֹת לִמְקוֹמָן.
phrases.english: and the other master holds: the sheep nature did not return to its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, בְּרָחֵל בַּת עֵז בַּת רָחֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second possible case that answers the same problem as Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בכורה reading seems to clash with 'אך בכור שור.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is whether a returning resemblance to the grandmother counts, so רבי מאיר is not ignoring the פסוק.

steps.title: רב אשי: an animal with only some of its mother's features
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the case is an animal that has only some of its mother's features. The חכמים who exempt it are רבי שמעון, who requires the head and most of the body to look like the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: the case is where it has some of the signs. And who are the חכמים? רבי שמעון, who said: not until its head and most of its body look like its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a third explanation. The newborn is partly like its mother, and the argument is how much resemblance is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, some of the mother's features are enough to count as the same kind for בכורה. The 'חכמים' are really רבי שמעון, who demands that the head and most of the body match the mother. So both sides accept 'אך בכור שור'; they only argue about how much matching it takes.

keyTerms.meaning: Its head and most of its body

steps.whatToRemember: All three answers keep רבי מאיר talking about בכורה, and none of them goes against 'אך בכור שור.' The argument is either which ancestor counts (Steps 14 and 15) or how much the newborn must resemble its mother (רב אשי).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
for example, where it has some of the signs,
phrases.notes: He means some of its mother's features, not all of them.

phrases.english: and who are the Sages? Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ דּוֹמֶה לְאִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: who said: not until its head and most of it look like its mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, independent way to set up the case, from רב אשי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case and identifying the unnamed חכמים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר seems to obligate an animal that does not resemble its mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: The newborn partly resembles its mother. רבי מאיר says that is enough, and רבי שמעון requires the head and most of the body to match.

steps.title: Even רבי מאיר requires the ראש חודש goat to come from a goat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that רבי מאיר agrees the שעיר of ראש חודש must be the child of a female goat, learned from the extra word ״אחד״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי מאיר agrees that for the goat of ראש חודש, we need the son of a female goat. What is the reason? The פסוק says ״אחד״ (one). This means it must be special and unchanged, coming down from the six days of creation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a new rule. Even רבי מאיר, who is lenient about animals that look different from their mothers, agrees that the ראש חודש goat must be a real goat born from a goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15's case, רבי מאיר treated an animal as a בכור even though it did not look like its mother, because it looked like its grandmother. Here רבי יוחנן limits that leniency. For the שעיר of ראש חודש, the word ״אחד״ teaches that the animal must be the 'one special' kind, the same species it has been since creation.

keyTerms.meaning: The male goat brought as a חטאת on ראש חודש
The son of a female goat

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי מאיר's leniency about mixed-looking animals has limits when a פסוק demands a pure species.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Rabbi Meir concedes
regarding the goat of the New Moon
that we require the son of a female goat,
What is the reason?
The verse says: "one"
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:15

phrases.english: one that is distinct and comes down
from the six days of creation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי מאיר's position from the earlier discussion by naming a case where he agrees to be strict.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to רבי מאיר, the שעיר of ראש חודש must be a goat born from a female goat, because ״אחד״ means the pure original species.

steps.title: Isn't this already learned from another פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ״אחד״ is needed, since the פסוק of ״שור או כשב או עז״ already excludes a mixed animal and one that looks like another species.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is this learned from here? It is learned from there: ״שור או כשב״ excludes a mixed breed, and ״או עז״ excludes an animal that looks like a different species.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's source. Another פסוק already teaches that an animal that looks like a different species cannot be a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא about animals born for קרבנות already excludes a נדמה, an animal that looks like a different kind. So the extra word ״אחד״ seems unnecessary. The challenge is about the source, not about the rule itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A mix of two species (here, an animal born from two kinds)
An animal that looks like a different species from its mother

phrases.english: But is it derived from here?
It is derived from there —
"a bull or a sheep" — to exclude a mixed breed,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:27

phrases.english: "or a goat" — to exclude one that looks like another species.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source רבי יוחנן used in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's use of ״אחד״ as the source for requiring a pure goat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק ״שור או כשב או עז״ already excludes a נדמה, so ״אחד״ seems unnecessary for this rule.

steps.title: Both פסוקים are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that each פסוק teaches something the other could not: ויקרא alone would not cover an animal that looks like an earlier generation, and ״אחד״ alone would only cover required offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If we only had the פסוק from there, I would think it applies only when the different look does not come from earlier generations, but when it does come from them, I would say it is allowed. And if we only had this פסוק, I would think it applies only to a required offering, but not to a voluntary one. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a צריכא: each פסוק covers a gap the other leaves open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא might only exclude an animal whose look comes from nowhere in its family line. ״אחד״ adds that even a look inherited from a grandparent disqualifies it. But ״אחד״ is said about a חובה offering, so we still need ויקרא to apply the rule to a נדבה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed: both sources teach something

steps.whatToRemember: Each פסוק adds its own rule. ויקרא excludes a נדמה even from a voluntary offering. ״אחד״ excludes it even when its look comes from earlier generations, for the required ראש חודש offering.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if only from there, I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא נְחַת לְדָרֵי,
phrases.english: this applies only where it does not go back to earlier generations,
phrases.notes: He means the animal's different look does not come from any parent or grandparent.

phrases.english: but where it does go back, say it does not apply.
And if only from here, I would have said:
this applies only to an obligatory offering,
but a voluntary offering — not,
so it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18 by showing that both פסוקים are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source covers a case the other would miss
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only ויקרא, a look inherited from earlier generations would be allowed. With only ״אחד״, a voluntary offering would be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both פסוקים are needed. ויקרא teaches that a נדמה is unfit even for a voluntary offering. ״אחד״ teaches that even a look that comes from earlier generations disqualifies it, as for the ראש חודש offering.

steps.title: No מלקות for כלאים with wool from a changed animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר יעקב says everyone agrees there are no מלקות for שעטנז using the wool of an animal that looks like another species, because wool is compared to linen, which does not change.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר יעקב said: Everyone agrees that one does not get lashes for its wool because of כלאים, as it says: ״לא תלבש שעטנז״. Just as linen has not changed, so too the wool must be from an animal that has not changed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement about the same kind of animal, now for the איסור of שעטנז. Wool from such an animal does not bring מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts wool next to linen. Linen is always just linen, so the wool must also come from an animal that is unchanged, one that looks like its own kind. Wool from a נדמה is outside the איסור that brings מלקות, and both sides of the earlier argument agree on this.

keyTerms.meaning: A garment of wool and linen together

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean such wool is fully allowed with linen. It only says there are no מלקות for it under the פסוק of שעטנז.

phrases.english: Rabbi Aḥa bar Yaakov said:
Everyone agrees that one is not flogged
for its wool on account of diverse kinds,
as it says: "You shall not wear shaatnez,"
phrases.notes: דברים 22:11

phrases.english: just as linen has not changed —
so too wool that has not changed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new series of rulings about an animal that looks like another species, now in the area of כלאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are no מלקות for שעטנז made with wool from a changed-looking animal, since the wool must be unchanged like linen.

steps.title: רב פפא: Such wool cannot be used for תכלת
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says everyone agrees that wool from an animal that looks like another species is פסול for תכלת, since ציצית is placed next to linen in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Everyone agrees that its wool is unfit for תכלת. The פסוק says, 'Do not wear שעטנז... make yourself twisted cords.' Just as linen has not changed, so too the wool must be from an animal that has not changed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a second ruling that uses the same 'compare wool to linen' idea from Step 20, this time for the blue threads of ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of ציצית comes right after the פסוק of שעטנז, which mentions wool and linen together. Linen always stays the same, so the wool used for ציצית must also come from an animal that did not 'change' into the look of another species.

keyTerms.meaning: The sky-blue wool used in ציצית

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Everyone agrees that its wool is unfit for sky-blue wool,
as it says: 'You shall not wear diverse kinds...
you shall make yourself twisted cords,'
just as linen has not changed,
so too, wool that has not changed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies Step 20's wool-like-linen comparison to תכלת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wool from an animal resembling another species is פסול for תכלת, even according to everyone.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: Such wool does not become impure with נגעים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says everyone agrees that a garment made of this wool cannot become טמא with נגעים, because the פסוק puts wool next to linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Everyone agrees that its wool does not become טמא with נגעים. The פסוק says, 'in a woolen garment or a linen garment.' Just as linen has not changed, so too the wool must be from an animal that has not changed.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא uses the same wool-and-linen comparison, now for the טומאה of a garment with a נגע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about garment נגעים lists wool and linen side by side. Since linen does not change, only wool from an animal that did not change can get this טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Leprous marks (צרעת) that can make a garment טמא

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים שֶׁאֵין צַמְרוֹ מִטַּמֵּא בִּנְגָעִים,
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that its wool does not become impure with leprous marks,
as it says: 'in a woolen garment or a linen garment,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:47

phrases.english: just as linen has not changed,
so too, wool that has not changed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel application of the same comparison, now to נגעים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wool from an animal resembling another species does not become טמא with נגעים, even according to everyone.

steps.title: רב אשי: Wine from a vine trained over a fig tree is unfit for libations
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי extends the 'unchanged' idea: wine from a vine trained over a fig tree is פסול for נסכים, since נסכים are paired with a זבח, which must be unchanged.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We can also say that if someone trained a grapevine over a fig tree, its wine is unfit for נסכים. Why? The פסוק says 'a זבח and נסכים.' Just as a זבח must be unchanged, so too the נסכים must be unchanged.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes the same kind of reasoning and applies it to a new area: wine poured on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the paired item is the animal offering, not linen. Since a קרבן must come from an animal that did not change, the wine that goes with it must also come from a vine that did not change, and growing over a fig tree counts as a change.

keyTerms.meaning: Trained a plant to climb over something
Wine libations poured on the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַף אָנוּ נֹאמַר,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: We too can say,
if one trained the grapevine over a fig tree,
its wine is unfit for libations.
What is the reason? 'An offering and libations':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:37

phrases.english: just as an offering has not changed,
so too, libations that have not changed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַף אָנוּ נֹאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the 'unchanged' principle from wool to wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine from a vine trained over a fig tree is פסול for נסכים.

steps.title: רבינא: Then flax over a bush would also be changed
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי: if training a plant over another counts as a change, flax trained over a bush should also be changed, and then we could not say linen 'does not change.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged this: If someone trained flax over a bush, would that also count as changed? If so, you could not say 'just as linen has not changed,' because linen can change too!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רב אשי's new rule by showing it would break the linen comparison used in Steps 20–22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole wool rule depends on linen being something that never changes. If growing one plant over another counts as a change, then flax can change too, and the comparison falls apart.

phrases.english: Ravina challenged it:
if one trained flax over a bush,
would it also be considered changed?
If so, you cannot say
'just as linen has not changed,'
phrases.notes: He is quoting the comparison רבי אחא בר יעקב used back in Step 20.

phrases.english: since linen also changes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's extension in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule that growing a vine over a fig tree is a 'change.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the same logic flax over a bush would change, which undermines the premise that linen never changes.

steps.title: רב אשי: The wine's smell changes, the flax's does not
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that wine from a vine over a fig tree takes on a different smell, but flax over a bush keeps its smell, so only the wine counts as changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This one's smell changed, and that one's smell did not change.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends his rule by showing a real difference between the wine and the flax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What makes something 'changed' here is a noticeable change, like smell. The wine picks up a new smell from the fig tree, but the flax stays the same, so linen still counts as unchanged and the comparison survives.
steps.whatToRemember: Wool from an animal that looks like another species is excluded from תכלת and נגעים because it is compared to unchanged linen. Wine from a vine over a fig tree is פסול for נסכים because its smell changes, while flax over a bush does not change.

phrases.english: He said to him: This one's scent changed,
phrases.notes: רב אשי is answering. 'This one' is the wine from the vine over the fig tree.

phrases.english: and that one's scent did not change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge in Step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any training of one plant over another counts as a change, so flax would change too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a change in smell counts. The wine changes, the flax does not, so linen remains 'unchanged.'

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: twin males born together both go to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes a first-time ewe that gives birth to two males whose heads come out together. רבי יוסי הגלילי rules that both lambs go to the כהן, based on the plural word הזכרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A ewe that never gave birth before had two male lambs, and both heads came out at the same time. רבי יוסי הגלילי says both lambs go to the כהן, because the פסוק says "the males are to ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a tricky case: twin male lambs whose heads come out at the same moment. רבי יוסי הגלילי gives the first opinion: both are a בכור and both go to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only one animal can be the first one born. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that if both heads truly come out together, both count as first. He supports this with the plural word הזכרים, "the males," which shows that more than one male can be a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, our משנה. It marks the start of a new משנה.
Had given birth before. Here it means this is her first birth.
"The males are to ה׳". The plural is the source for רבי יוסי הגלילי.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A ewe that had not given birth before
and it gave birth to two males
and both their heads came out at once
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says
both of them go to the kohen
as it is stated: "The males are to the Lord"
phrases.notes: שמות 13:12. Notice the plural, "males"; that is his whole proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָחֵל שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרָה וְיָלְדָה שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is unrelated to רב אשי's discussion of wine and flax.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, twin males born at the same moment are both a בכור and both go to the כהן.

steps.title: חכמים: exact timing is impossible, so the כהן gets one
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree. Two births can never happen at exactly the same moment, so one lamb came first. The owner keeps one lamb and the כהן gets one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: it is impossible for them to come out at exactly the same instant. Rather, one goes to the owner and one goes to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים argue with רבי יוסי הגלילי. They say one lamb really came out first, even if we could not see it, so the כהן gets only one lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about what really happened, not about the פסוק. חכמים hold that two events can never happen at precisely the same moment, so only one lamb is the true בכור. We do not know which one came first, and that doubt sets up the next argument about which lamb the כהן takes.

keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible to be exact. Two events cannot happen at precisely the same instant.
A doubt. Here, we do not know which lamb is the בכור.

steps.confusionAlert: חכמים are not saying neither lamb is a בכור. One of them definitely is. We just do not know which one, and that is why the כהן gets only one.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule אי אפשר לצמצם, that perfect timing cannot happen, is a famous principle used in other places in ש״ס too.

phrases.english: And the Sages say
it is impossible to be precise
phrases.notes: They mean the two heads could not have come out at the exact same instant. One was first, even if nobody could tell.

phrases.english: rather, one is for him and one is for the kohen
phrases.notes: "Him" is the owner of the ewe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רבי יוסי הגלילי in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since two births cannot be exactly simultaneous, only one lamb is a בכור, so the owner keeps one and the כהן takes one.

steps.title: רבי טרפון: the כהן picks the better lamb
steps.stepSummary: Following חכמים, the כהן gets one lamb. רבי טרפון says the כהן chooses whichever lamb is nicer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: the כהן chooses the nicer one for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: This opinion goes with חכמים, who give the כהן one lamb. רבי טרפון answers the next question: which lamb does the כהן take? His answer is the better one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we do not know which lamb is the real בכור, someone has to decide which lamb the כהן gets. רבי טרפון gives the choice to the כהן, so he can take the nicer lamb.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon says
the kohen chooses the better one for himself

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּהֵן בּוֹרֵר לוֹ אֶת הַיָּפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on חכמים's view in step 27 and raises a new question: which lamb goes to the כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן chooses the better of the two lambs.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: they assess the lambs; the owner's lamb grazes until blemished
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי טרפון. The lambs are assessed between the owner and the כהן. The remaining lamb must graze until it gets a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: they assess the lambs between them. And the second lamb must graze until it becomes blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a different way to decide which lamb goes to the כהן: the lambs are assessed between the two sides. The משנה then says what happens to the second lamb: it must graze until it gets a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not let the כהן simply take the best lamb. Instead, the lambs are assessed between them, and the גמרא will explain exactly how this works. The owner's lamb might be the real בכור, so he cannot treat it as ordinary. He must wait until it gets a מום before he can use it.

keyTerms.meaning: They assess or estimate between them. The גמרא will explain the details.
It must graze. It is left in the pasture.
Until it becomes blemished, meaning it gets a מוּם
A blemish that makes a בכור unfit for the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: There are three steps in this משנה: (1) רבי יוסי הגלילי says both lambs go to the כהן. חכמים say only one, because אי אפשר לצמצם. (2) For the כהן's lamb, רבי טרפון says the כהן picks the better one, and רבי עקיבא says the lambs are assessed between them. (3) The leftover lamb is a possible בכור, so it grazes until it gets a מום.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says
they assess between them
and the second must graze until it becomes blemished
phrases.notes: "The second" is the lamb the owner keeps. It might be the real בכור, so he has to wait for a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רבי טרפון in step 28 and adds the rule for the owner's remaining lamb.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lambs are assessed between the owner and the כהן, and the owner's lamb, a possible בכור, must graze until it gets a מום.
